rationale: THE PROJECT'S OWN DECLARATIONS, the two that make the lane's rules bite. This file lives in a sub-directory, so the runner gives it a real project index (JAVA_DECLARATION_SPEC, complete=true) — the fail-closed rules need it. It declares the simple names the importing file uses: `Tool` TWICE (two nested classes, so the project's key space gives the name MORE THAN ONE answer and the name-keyed resolver TIES), `Unique` ONCE (the key space answers it uniquely, so the name model RESOLVES it and a claim there would trade a resolution for a claim), and `Own` TWICE (the tie holds, but the import names the PROJECT's own type, so the claim is refused on externality, not on the tie). Each refusal is pinned in ToolOwners.expectation.json; this file is the other half of the pair — the declarations those refusals are measured against.
